newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken Q3 earnings may miss target.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken Q3 earnings may miss target.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc said Wednesday third quarter earnings could be lower than expected as a result of a store sales decline which is expected to bottom out in the third quarter.

The company said it also expects "choppy" store performances during its transition period, which began in the second quarter, as it shifts its marketing strategy, slows development and streamlines the company to reduce costs.

The company said it expects annual savings of about $10 million at its support center, and its area developers expect annual savings of about $30 million as a result of the organizational streamlining.
In addition, the company said lower store sales and margins could mean losses for its financed area developers will increase in 1997 over 1996 levels.
However, the company expects to see improvement in store performance later in the year as it begins a "unified marketing and advertising program."

The company reported second quarter earnings per share of $0.26 compared with $0.24 for the same period a year ago. The second quarter earnings per share were $0.29 before one-time charges related to the organizational streamlining.
The company's revenue rose to $116.6 million from $64.6 million as a result of an increase in the number of company-operated stores from 79 to 227 at the end of the second quarter of 1997.
Greater royalties and franchise fees on a larger base of systemwide sales also contributed to the higher revenue.
